recent.narrative: Late evening thunderstorms caused by a pre-frontal trough tracked southeast out of Canada and across the north country on June 13th. A few of these storms were severe as they tracked into the forecast area.

recent.area: ST LAWRENCE RIVER FROM OGDENSBURG TO ST REGIS NY
recent.narrative: Ahead of a cold front, a broken line of thunderstorms formed on Tuesday evening from southern Ontario to northern Ohio. Eventually these storm storms moved east across our area, resulting in wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph Lake Erie, 30 to 40 mph on Lake Ontario, and nearly 50 mph along the St. Lawrence River.

recent.narrative: An upper level trough and a strong lake breeze combined with an unstable air mass to trigger a line of thunderstorms from Southern Ontario to western Pennsylvania. These storms increased in coverage and intensity as they swept eastward across western and North Central New York late afternoon into the evening.

recent.area: ST LAWRENCE RIVER ABOVE OGDENSBURG NY
recent.narrative: A cold front was to our west and stalled out. A highly unstable air mass in place. Two rounds of severe weather occurred. The first was over the North Country and St. Lawrence Valley and aided by a well-developed vortex that had traversed the Toronto area early in the afternoon. The lake breeze off of Lake Erie protected the Buffalo metro area, but it ultimately interacted with the lake breeze and instability to the east of Lake Ontario. These storms produced mostly large hail. A second round of severe storms occurred later in the evening as a couple of passing waves triggered thunderstorms due to very high instability. Wind damage and heavy rain with some flooding were the main issues. Most of this was from the Genesee Valley to the west as thunderstorms weakened once they pushed eastward after midnight.

recent.area: ST LAWRENCE RIVER ABOVE OGDENSBURG NY
recent.narrative: A cold front dropped from north to south across the area. Unstable conditions were evident ahead of this, with about 2000 J/kg CAPE developing by late afternoon. Moderate mid-level shear was present with a shortwave just ahead of the front. Storms developed ahead of this frontal boundary around 3 PM and along a lake breeze boundary in Niagara County. Impressive cores aloft were quickly evident as they developed. These cells kept redeveloping back to the west, with several impressive cores aloft prompting multiple warnings. These produced numerous reports of large hail, including tennis ball sized hail Storms also trained along the boundary, producing heavy rainfall in the same location. This produced significant flash flooding in Lockport and surrounding areas.
